opportunity: ActionHideShadow, the upstream merge-phalanx pass that consolidates two copies of one value into a single chain so the repeated assignment stops printing, was scheduled in kuna but its body was a no-op stub. Its engine half, Merge::hide_shadows, was already a complete port. The stub named three blockers -- a written def-set iterator, the HighVariable mark surface and the MergeContext bridge -- and all three exist today.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-hideshadow.xml (3 assertions: off = the repeated copy, on = one copy, plus a guard function whose two copies sit on exclusive branches and must survive ON) + 3 option-parse unit tests
root_cause: The action body was never wired, so hide_shadows was dead code. Wiring it is the whole change: walk the written def-set, dedup HighVariables through the bank mark bit, call Merge::hide_shadows. The one non-transcription decision is the Cover read: C++ Varnode::getCover() lazily rebuilds a dirtied cover and kuna's MergeContext::vn_cover_ref is a plain field read, while the previous iteration's op_set_input is exactly what dirties it -- so the pass calls MergeContext::bank_update_cover before each containment test. Measured: the binaries that change are byte-identical with and without that refresh, so no corpus decision depended on a stale cover.
what_changes_in_the_c: One assignment statement disappears. No declaration disappears -- the variable survives, only the redundant write to it goes -- so varcensus reports a zero delta and this is a statement-count item, not a declaration-count item.

firing_census.method: instrumented build, 40 stripped ELFs at O0 and O2 (coreutils ls/sort/fmt/cp/du/dd/date/cat/head/printf, grep, gzip, diffutils x4, bzip2 x2, findutils, tar)
firing_census.note: most accepted re-points hit a COPY the printer already suppresses (the for-loop initialize/iterate ops marked non-printing by funcdata_block.rs:567,571), which is why far fewer than 110 reach the text

corpus_ab.arms: kuna decompile-all <bin> --option hideshadow off|on (explicit on both arms, so the shipped default does not affect the measurement)

varcensus.method: scripts.pipeline.varcensus, off vs on, on the binaries that change
varcensus.why: the pass removes a write, never a declaration

speed.method: scripts.pipeline.timeit (median of 15) for the single function; interleaved off/on pairs, MINIMUM of the pairs, for whole-binary decompile-all; an off-vs-off control run on the same binary to establish the noise floor

rows.CONTROL kuna decompile-all coreutils/ls: 13984 -> 13794 ms (-1.36%), i.e. the noise floor on this box is about +/-1.4%

speed.note: an earlier ls O2 pair measured +4.63% while the box was at load 30 with a concurrent workspace test run and a 444-slice sweep; re-measured against its own off-vs-off control it is +0.11%

typesweep_small.slices: 27 (grep, gzip, diffutils, bzip2, findutils at O0, O2, O2-noinline)

json_surface.method: kuna decompile-all --json off vs on on all 10 binaries whose C changes, comparing every function's variables[] field-by-field
json_surface.fields_that_differ: line_numbers only (shifted by one, because a line was deleted)
json_surface.fields_that_are_identical: name, type, size, kind, arg_index, stack_offset, addresses -- i.e. every field type_match scores
json_surface.conclusion: structurally neutral on type_match by construction; the measured sweep agrees

typesweep_changed_projects.slices: 276 (coreutils + shadow at O2 and O2-noinline -- every project whose C this option changes at those levels)
